newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHEARER, GASCOIGNE AND SEAMAN BOOST ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHEARER, GASCOIGNE AND SEAMAN BOOST ENGLAND.

text.p: England were given a boost before Wednesday's vital World Cup qualifier against Italy when captain Alan Shearer, midfielder Paul Gascoigne and goalkeeper David Seaman reported no new injury problems after coming through a training session on Monday.

But the news surrounding England's three other injured players was not so positive as centreback Tony Adams (ankle), midfielder Paul Ince (thigh) and midfielder Robert Lee (groin) are still major doubts for the group two match at Wembley.

Hoddle said: "The six lads all stepped up their training today. Three came through with flying colours: Alan Shearer, Paul Gascoigne and David Seaman. I just hope there's no reaction with Alan Shearer's lower back ... but fingers crossed it's looking good.
"Tony Adams did some lighter training and the same goes for Paul Ince and Robert Lee, so we have three positives and three not so.''
Hoddle added: "Tony trained on his own today and is still feeling a sore ankle. Paul, has still got a thigh problem and couldn't join in with the group work.
"I'd love to say he's come through fine, but although he's worked extremely hard he still hasn't convinced himself he's fit to train properly."
Gascoigne damaged ankle ligaments playing for Rangers in a six-a-side tournament in Amsterdam two weeks ago, while Shearer has a back injury and Seaman is recovering from an injured knee.
Hoddle basically imposed a deadline of Tuesday afternoon for the players to prove their fitness, saying he wanted to get the shape of his team formed in his head before Wednesday.
England go into the match with three wins from their three opening qualifiers while Italy have won their two qualifiers to date.
The Italians are due to arrive in London later on Monday and will have their first training session at Wembley on Tuesday morning.
